summary: We made a really cool and interesting thing.
details: For this project, we chose a task titled "Dancing with the SARs"—because dancing is fun! We started by looking at various photos and videos of dancing. We selected "Verity" as the character to do the dancing; to be honest, I don’t know who that is, but the kids on my team insisted that it’s something very popular. Next, we had to create a dance animation. Gemini helped us with this (I just hope it has no connection to China!). I believe this will help draw children's attention to global issues. Just you wait—thanks to this, the 2027 hackathon will have far more participants than the 2026 one. Beyond SI, we relied on a number of sophisticated tools to bring this to life—specifically, Microsoft PowerPoint. It was in this very application that we managed to create a dance animation from nine individual frames—an animation that, if I recall correctly, was even used elsewhere in the project. As previously mentioned, the goal of this project is to help engage the younger generation in the development of NASA space initiatives. Its true creativity lies in the fact that absolutely no one else would ever do something like this.
